target_customer: Gen Z and young millennial women aged about 15 to 30 who buy and sell secondhand clothing
problem: Young women want cheap fashion and a way to resell clothes from a phone without holding inventory or going through clunky marketplaces.
business_model: Peer-to-peer marketplace with a take rate on each sale (the YC page says 20 percent; a search snippet shows a 1 dollar plus 5 percent fee, so the fee has changed)

founders.name: David Oates
founders.background_notes: Wikipedia lists Sara Kiparizoska, David Oates, William Ault and Eli Allen as founders and says Kiparizoska and Ault studied at the University of Mississippi when designing the app.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile marketplace with listings, payments and shipping labels is standard consumer engineering.

defensibility.rationale: A seller and buyer network helps, but larger resale apps already existed and users can multi-home.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The January 2021 article calls ThredUp and Poshmark sizable competitors and notes eBay has a similar listing-image tool. No acquisition of Curtsy found.

market_need_then: Retail Dive reported 85,000 items sold in October 2020, up 35 percent from September, and the company says it has over 4 million community members and a 4.8 rating on over 565K App Store ratings. No 2016 demand data was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Fashion resale. For the girls (site tagline); CEO said in 2021 they were working on a strong brand voice.

rebrands.why: Wikipedia says the company was previously known as Nimble; no reason or date found.

branding.community_and_virality: Company reports 4 million plus community members and a Try Ons video feature; no independent press on the brand found.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly feminine name that suits the audience, a very high app rating and a stated focus on brand voice, but no independent evidence that the brand drove growth.

pivots.from: Peer-to-peer dress rental for sorority members
pivots.why: Retail Dive says it shifted to buying and selling after being accepted into Y Combinator.

outcome_analysis: Curtsy pivoted from sorority dress rental to resale in 2016, raised an 11 million dollar Series A led by Index Ventures in January 2021 and still operates with about 15 people listed by YC. It sold 85,000 items in October 2020. Funding before 2021 is only partly known, and a fashionunited report of 14.5 million total was seen only in search results, so total capital is uncertain.
notes: Series A reported by Retail Dive (opened) and several outlets in search snippets (FashionUnited, Marketscreener, TechCrunch). A FashionUnited snippet puts total funding at 14.5 million, implying about 3.5 million earlier; that earlier round was not found. Wikipedia mentions 120,000 dollars for 7 percent equity from YC and Rebel Venture Capital without dates; it is not recorded as a round. YC lists two founders while Wikipedia lists four. No competitor source dated near the 2016 batch was found; the Poshmark and ThredUp mentions are from 2021 and kept out of the list.
